scope: Global South and non-Western biennials: Sharjah Biennial 16 (2025), 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo (2025), Dak'Art 2024, Kochi-Muziris Biennale 2025-26, Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024 and 2026, documenta fifteen (2022), Bangkok Art Biennale 2024. Every record comes from a page I read. Descriptions paraphrased. Where a source did not state a field it is null.

exhibitions.name: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
exhibitions.city: Sharjah (United Arab Emirates), 17 venues incl. Al Mureijah Art Spaces, Al Dhaid, Al Hamriyah, Kalba, Al Madam
exhibitions.artistic_director: Five co-curators: Alia Swastika, Amal Khalaf, Megan Tamati-Quennell, Natasha Ginwala, Zeynep Oz (Sharjah Art Foundation director: Hoor Al Qasimi)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: 'to carry' asks what people bring with them when they travel, flee, survive or stay: histories, stories, cultures, burdens, futures. A critic links it to Ursula K. Le Guin's carrier bag essay; the same critic notes that carrying also transforms.
sections: No named sections. Five curatorial strands instead: women's knowledge and speculative technological futures (Swastika)
Storytelling and song as rituals of collective learning (Khalaf)
Indigenous perspectives on land and reciprocity (Tamati-Quennell)
Societal systems shaped by technology, incl. 'Farm Project' of six audio pieces (Oz)
critic_notes: E-flux critic found the show incoherent: any line of curatorial inquiry is dropped or contradicted, a result of five curators with different commitments, but he reads this as fitting for a messy time.
Same critic names a 'queasy genre': local craftspeople recruited by a visiting artist to make a textile work on a set topic, which yields what a mid-2020s biennial piece is expected to look and mean.

Same critic argues politically charged archives (Photo Kegham) work best when they are not dressed up as art, and that activist painting (Richard Bell) looks bland in a museum beside strong painting (Muriati).

Artlink critic: Bait Al Serkal became a 'walk-in wunderkammer' of cultural objects, so decolonising intent was overshadowed and works were almost re-exoticised; instruments in a poorly lit listening room stood in for a living Nairobi collective.
Artlink critic also notes absences: gender politics, queer theory and disability are quiet; few Western names, almost all Global South.
Architectural Paper critic: seams between curators are nearly invisible; best when work answers the building (roofless house, 1970s clinic, mud-brick house); not every work feels substantial.
Many works treat ancient craft and ancestral knowledge as valuable for their own sake, which one critic finds uncritical next to a mock-ethnographic artifact display.

exhibitions.name: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
exhibitions.city: Sao Paulo (Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion, Ibirapuera Park, designed by Oscar Niemeyer)
exhibitions.artistic_director: Bonaventure Soh Bejeng Ndikung (chief curator), with Alya Sebti, Anna Roberta Goetz, Thiago de Paula Souza; Keyna Eleison curator-at-large
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Title comes from a poem by Afro-Brazilian writer Conceicao Evaristo ('Da calma e do silencio'): some travellers do not walk roads, there are submerged worlds that only poetry can enter. The subtitle treats humanity as a verb and a practice. The central curatorial image is the estuary, where rivers meet the sea.
sections: Frequencies of Landings and Belongings (also reported as Frequencies of Arrivals and Belongings)
Currents of Nurturing and Plural Cosmologies (Flows of Care and Plural Cosmologies)
The Intractable Beauty of the World
critic_notes: Several critics find the theme so all-encompassing that almost any work could be included; one gallerist at the opening said she did not understand it.

Wall texts are mostly absent from works. Descriptions sit on circular panels at columns, and the map lists names only, no titles. A critic calls this a sharp but frustrating gesture, another a curatorial overstep.

ArtReview praises spatial generosity and strong commissions but finds the long orange, turquoise and green curtains act as scenic drapery hiding temporary walls, and the weakest works occupy the atrium.
Art Newspaper (4 stars for works, 3 for show): lyrical and sometimes muddled, 'alienating to everyone'; strongest when nature is a metaphor and in the performance programme.
E-flux: tendency toward immersive, sensorial installations (veils, sound, colour blocks); optimism felt out of step with the political moment; Gaza addressed only obliquely.
Okoyomon's entrance garden is read as spectacle: a costly temporary garden next to a permanent park visible through the glass wall.
More than half of the works are new commissions; fewer than one in four artists is Brazilian.

exhibitions.name: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
exhibitions.city: Dakar (Ancien Palais de Justice, Musee des Civilisations Noires, Galerie Nationale d'Art)
exhibitions.artistic_director: Salimata Diop (first woman in the role), with curators Kara Blackmore, Marynet J, Cindy Olohou
exhibitions.title_metaphor: The Wake: partly inspired by Christina Sharpe's book 'In the Wake: On Blackness and Being' (2016); the trilingual title (French, English, Wolof) is meant to stay open to several readings: awakening, wake of a ship, mourning vigil. Diop describes artists as sentinels of the imagination who dig new river beds.
critic_notes: Flash Art: lighting washes and projections turn the old courthouse into 'a journey through Atlantis', but giving most rooms to one artist weakens the planned shared experience; ocean imagery is thin in the work.
Flash Art: placing Ulysse's piece on the facade repeats a familiar biennial gesture and risks being decoration rather than a confrontation with the building's colonial history.
Contemporary Lynx: uneven quality in huge venues; many diaspora artists are European- or American-based and sponsored by large galleries; national pavilions (Senegal) can feel like tourist postcards.
Contemporary Lynx: official language of awakening and ecology is not matched by conditions on the ground; no dialogue between artists and politicians.
Berlin Art Link: several tech works did not function at the opening; strongest pieces are water, memory and ritual themed.
Postponed six months (from May) by the political unrest that followed the presidential election.

exhibitions.name: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
exhibitions.city: Kochi, Kerala (22 venues in Fort Kochi and Mattancherry; Aspinwall House, Anand Warehouse, Pepper House, Island Warehouse on Willingdon Island)
exhibitions.artistic_director: Nikhil Chopra with the collective HH Art Spaces
exhibitions.title_metaphor: 'For the Time Being' means provisional, in-between, unfinished; the curators say they want to explore the idea of the unfinished spectacle and call the event a living ecosystem. A critic notes it echoes the Hindi 'chalta hai' (let it be). Dec 12, 2025 to Mar 31, 2026.
sections: No fixed sections; core show plus associated platforms: Students' Biennale, Invitations, Collaterals, Special Projects (eight platforms in all)
critic_notes: E-flux: many venues were half-finished at opening, with grinders and scissor lifts beside works; the 'unfinished' concept blurs with production failure, yet the work, often new commissions, was excellent, especially delicate pieces about structures in collapse.
ArtReview: reads the title as nuanced evasion; spots familiar art-world habits: cosmopolitan privilege styled as exile, love of exegesis, naive faith in 'the body' as universal ground.

STIR: compares opening to a wedding feast where produce is still arriving; works arrive, change and leave over 110 days; a performance of omens and divination split viewers between spellbound and gimmicky.
Art Asia Pacific: process-based theme with many performances; strong long-form video; commended for hosting Pakistani, Bangladeshi and Palestinian artists.
A controversy arose over a figurative painting of nuns at a table in an associated show, which was withdrawn.

exhibitions.name: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
exhibitions.city: Riyadh, JAX District (Diriyah), former warehouse zone
exhibitions.title_metaphor: After Rain: petrichor, the smell of rain on dry earth, as a metaphor for renewal and cleansing; water also as scarce resource. The first edition (2021, Philip Tinari) was also water themed.
critic_notes: ARTnews: overwhelming presence of Gulf and South Asian artists is a credit; quality varies and biennial veterans outperform; odd installation choices in a new venue.

ARTnews: standout work looks back as well as forward, which sits uneasily with the state-led reinvention drive that funds the show; a biennial as a metaphor for renewal exposes its sponsor to scrutiny.

ARTnews: the best section is the previous generation of Saudi and Gulf women artists in 'Modern Legacies and Geopolitics', e.g. textile collage and craft research, which share a note of eulogy for folk heritage.
Sotheby's staff note each hall has its own smell and special lighting, so the visit is not only visual.

exhibitions.name: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
exhibitions.city: Riyadh, JAX District (Diriyah); Jan 30 to May 2, 2026
exhibitions.artistic_director: Nora Razian and Sabih Ahmed (co-artistic directors); exhibition design Sammy Zarka; scenography Formafantasma
exhibitions.title_metaphor: In Interludes and Transitions (Arabic: fi al-hill wa al-tarhal, a phrase for settling and journeying): the movements, migrations and transformations that link the Arab region to the wider world; geography as relation, identity as circulation.
sections: No named sections reported; sequence of spatial transitions across halls and courtyards
critic_notes: Hube: scenography of heavy platforms, plinths and wall panelling feels institutional and at odds with the theme of flux; works are lifted from the ground and become props.
Hube: invokes Glissant (opacity), Bauman (liquid modernity) and Said; the quieter works (gauze forms, scores, drawings of vitrines) persuade most.
ArchDaily: Formafantasma describe floating planes, textile elements and curved canvases used instead of walls; over 25 new commissions across a 12,900 sq m campus.

exhibitions.name: documenta fifteen
exhibitions.city: Kassel (32 venues across four districts, incl. Fridericianum, documenta Halle, Hubner Areal, Hallenbad Ost, WH22, Karlsaue)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: lumbung is the Indonesian word for a communal rice barn where surplus harvest is stored and shared. It became the model for pooling resources, ideas and decisions. ruangrupa invited lumbung members, who invited others, so the artist count grew to around 1,500.
sections: No sections; lumbung members, lumbung artists, ruruHaus (a living room for Kassel), lumbung Kios (shared kiosk network), working groups
critic_notes: ArtAsiaPacific: despite the scandals, a treat to meet collectives and scenes that stay distant otherwise; ideals of redistribution felt exactly right after the pandemic.
Momus: critics wrote around the word 'lumbung' as if it were an exotic dish; much coverage was news, not criticism; the model itself was blamed for the controversies.

Wallpaper: free-market stalls in the Fridericianum looked good on paper but visitors did not talk across tables; artists from the Global South worked for a mostly white audience; lumbung needs far more than a weekend.
Wallpaper: few static, object-based works exist in a mostly living and changing event; The Nest Collective's cubes are one such outstanding piece.
A Taring Padi banner with antisemitic imagery was covered and removed two days after opening; the director general resigned; one critic said the show's aim and its downfall was 'vibing'.

exhibitions.name: Bangkok Art Biennale 2024: Nurture Gaia
exhibitions.city: Bangkok (11 venues incl. National Museum, National Gallery, BACC, One Bangkok), Oct 24, 2024 to Feb 25, 2025
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Nurture Gaia: Greek earth goddess; nature and nurture, femininity and feminine values, ecopolitics, animism. (Curator names not read in my sources.)
critic_notes: art4d selected seven works about nature, femininity and ecology; four of the eleven venues were new, and the museum lent artefacts to sit beside new art.
Inflatable and stainless steel sculpture draw crowds for photographs, which art4d reads as an echo of fast urban life.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Al Mureijah Square, newly built gallery beside Comilang's piece, Sharjah
works.title: Gastromancer
works.what_you_see: A queue forms outside a circular room that glows red. Inside, two big red fibreglass murex shells hang in the air, and the visitor stands between them to hear voices coming from the open cavities. The room is lit and enclosed like a chapel.
nonvisual: sound: spoken dialogue from the shells about a forced change of sex
claims: The shells say they changed from female to male because of tributyltin, a toxic red hull paint, and so cannot breed.
The work criticises ecological harm from constant resource extraction, in a poetic way.
works.photo_notes: Published as a portrait of the artist with the work; not an installation shot.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Al Madam Buried Village (about an hour from Sharjah city), among sand-filled abandoned houses
works.title: Brier Patch
works.what_you_see: Rows of school desks are laid out in a grid inside the sand-filled shells of abandoned houses in a desert village. Each desk has tangled cedar branches growing out of it like a thicket. The setting is a ghost settlement, so the desks look like classroom ruins.
claims: Reimagines the classroom as a place of constraint and struggle.
Raises exclusion, assimilation and the limits of social mobility in the US.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Unrenovated roofless house with leafy courtyard, Al Mureijah
works.title: Jatibonic (People of Sacred High Waters)
works.what_you_see: Light falls through the roof gaps of a house left unrenovated. Beeswax candles hang in dense clusters along the walls while a woman keeps dipping wicks in hot wax. Taino figures stand beside woven rushes and ceramic thorns around a fire.
nonvisual: scent: smoke grows stronger as you go in
performance: candle making goes on all day
workshop: pottery made with Taller Cabachuelas, an Indigenous studio
claims: Revives Taino ancestral knowledge through apprenticeship and self-organised learning.
Candles, rushes and thorns stand for resilience, ceremony and cultural restoration.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Old Al Jubail Vegetable Market, Sharjah
works.title: Storage of the Broken Times-Ig Ritu
works.what_you_see: A round, airy structure for community gatherings sits at the middle of an old vegetable market. Around it are other installations, including a video called The Full Moon (2022) about elephants and people. The market is used as a spiritual gathering space.
claims: Sets up a dialogue between Sharjah, Assam and Bihar.
Evokes India's seasons and the changing lives of farming communities facing climate change.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Al Mureijah Art Spaces, Sharjah (nearby mosques audible)
works.title: Dub Plants
works.what_you_see: A tall radio tower built of bamboo and palm fronds stands in the open, with speakers fixed to it. It is one of the first things a visitor meets in the old centre. The sound mixes with the call to prayer from mosques next door.
nonvisual: sound: a composition that cites radio history, from Marconi's 1920 Thames broadcast to a pirated recording of Egyptian healing chants
claims: Links radio culture with agriculture.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.title: Saturated Salty Mud Stories
works.what_you_see: Three bodies of work are shown together as one installation. Oil and gas pipelines become large sprawling sculptures; ancient Islamic oil and perfume vessels are remade in glass; and a set of ceramics is glazed with materials partly gathered in Sharjah.
claims: Treats nature as both resource and battleground; trade, colonialism and migration are the themes.
Pipeline sculptures nod to the UAE's energy economy.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.artist: Kegham Djeghalian Sr (archive); Kegham Djeghalian Jr (reconstruction)
works.title: Photo Kegham of Gaza: Unboxing
works.what_you_see: An archive of studio photographs from Gaza: family portraits and holiday snaps from 1944 onward. One image shows a smiling boy on a sand dune with a barbed wire fence between him and the sea. The pictures are shown plainly, with little added text.
claims: The son uses the archive to rebuild a partial visual history of Gaza and to trace a scattered diaspora.
A critic says the biennial shelters cultures threatened with erasure.
themes: Sr founded the first professional photo studio in Gaza

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.title: Pool of Perspectives - 2030
works.what_you_see: An empty swimming pool is lined with digitally printed azulejo tiles. The tiles recall the Portuguese colonial presence in the Gulf and also mimic the glossy look of architectural renderings. It sits in an agricultural town far from the city.
claims: Hints at the wasteful megaprojects across the UAE.
works.photo_notes: Installation view with credit to Motaz Mawid; shows the tiled pool.

works.exhibition: Sharjah Biennial 16: to carry
works.venue_room: Calligraphy Square, reconstructed historic centre, Sharjah
works.title: The Tale of Dyah Tantri
works.what_you_see: A story-painting in Kamasan (Balinese puppet theatre) style. The surface is cut into an unstable grid by bands of bright colour patterned like flower garlands. In each panel humans, animals and monsters dance. The companion work Kusamba's War (2024), ink and poster paint on canvas, is 144 x 202 cm.
claims: A critic reads it as both visually striking and worth long looking, and as a serial storybook form like a comic or polyptych.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.title: Sun of Consciousness. God Blow Thru Me - Love Break Me
works.what_you_see: A spiral path of moss-covered earth runs past slowly browning trees, a stream that ends in a pond with fish, waterfalls and jets of mist. It fills the pavilion entrance, with the real park visible through the tall glass wall behind. Visitors wander and compare the indoor garden with the one outside.
nonvisual: sound: occasional bird calls and recorded nature sounds
claims: Catalogue draws parallels between a Brazilian biome and humanity and offers calm against chaos.
Comments on corporations extracting from the earth and on the social idea of 'nature'.
works.photo_notes: Press photos by Levi Fanan are wide installation views; Art Newspaper caption lists moss-covered earth and waterfalls.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.title: Orchestra Catastrophe: Act I (also catastrophe orchestra #1 (Act 1))
works.medium_line: Wood, matchboxes, matchsticks, paper, pigments, water, nylon ropes, sisal ropes, charcoal, debris, metal, leather, drums, automation mechanism with motor, clay, copper wires, audio cables, loudspeakers
works.what_you_see: A walk-in installation of matchbox panels glued into big planes, hand-made leather atabaque drums, and hunks of coal hung from the ceiling on cords like pendants. Motors swing the coal against the drums. Shards of coal sit on upturned speakers and shake apart under deep bass.
nonvisual: sound: bass vibration moves through the body
the sound of the room is recorded live and amplified, so a louder crowd makes the work fall into noise
claims: Matchboxes are used as percussion by samba musicians in Salvador.
Points to violent mineral extraction in Africa that supplies phones and electronics.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.title: Someone's Child
works.what_you_see: Large bronze and cement humanoid figures fill a room. They stand on the floor and perch on wall ledges like Catholic saints, each holding an oversize trumpet. They ring a snake-like being that wears two hat shapes.
claims: A critic reads the figures as both frightening and attractive, with sacred overtones.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.venue_room: Ramp and all three floors of the pavilion
works.title: A Casa de Bene (Bene's House)
works.what_you_see: Nine tall wooden columns wrapped in textile and leather rebuild the demolished house of her great-grandfather. The columns are wedged between floor and ceiling and run through the floors, so a column cut at one ceiling carries on below. Small objects sit among them: a vine, a bullet-shaped lighter, a bamboo basket, a gourd, sticks, a wooden box, charcoal and stones.
claims: Rebuilds a family house from a mining-damaged town in Minas Gerais.
The artist says the objects are pieces left from her great-grandfather's house.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.venue_room: Pavilion floor, staged white-cube space with Isa Genzken mannequins
works.title: Gallery 2
works.what_you_see: Large kraft paper sheets, painted white, are hung to copy the walls of a white cube gallery. The room is both painting and architecture. Camp mannequins in tagged clothes by Isa Genzken stand in the same staged cube.
claims: Critic: criticises the power that shapes institutional space and the reach of painting.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.title: Terra Viva (Living Earth)
works.what_you_see: Soil, plant resins and minerals, raw and processed, are set in glass cabinets and on shelves like a natural history lab, with lab equipment and handwritten notes. One report instead describes suspended textiles dyed with native plants and minerals, so published accounts differ.
claims: Shows earth as source of care and as victim of exploitation, with beauty.

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.title: Iroko: A arvore cosmica (Iroko: The Cosmic Tree)
works.what_you_see: Bronze casts of women warriors and bird women, each with a human body and a bird's head and wings, are arranged around a glowing yellow beaded tree. Some hold weapons, others hold gifts, and all wear jewellery.
claims: Critic: bronze strength and bead fragility show women as warriors and as enslaved people.
references: balangandans worn at the waist during slavery

works.exhibition: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo: Not All Travellers Walk Roads - Of Humanity as Practice
works.venue_room: Casa do Povo, Sao Paulo (programme outside the pavilion)
works.title: Batucada
works.what_you_see: Masked performers start to drum slowly on pots and oil cans and nudge the audience as they circle the room. The beat and the contact grow more intense until the performers take off their clothes. The hour-long piece ends in a room that smells of sweat, and the audience leaves around the performers' bodies.
nonvisual: performance: one hour of rising percussion
claims: Critic: uses Afro-Brazilian drumming to speak to power struggles without being didactic.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.venue_room: Facade and entrance of Ancien Palais de Justice
works.title: For Those Among Us Who Inherited Sacrifice, Rasanblaj!
works.what_you_see: A large wall of calabash and shells stands outside the entrance. Below it is a sea bed of stones. Looking up, the visitor sees a vertical wake that carries shells like oxygen bubbles and tribute baskets.
claims: Rasanblaj means a gathering of ideas, things, people and spirits: ceremony, protest, assembly.
A critic reads it as a ritual of adapting to warming and flooding.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.venue_room: Corridor in the Ancien Palais de Justice
works.title: Méditez-rat-n'est-rien
works.what_you_see: Eighty-eight abstract paintings in acrylic and natural pigment on paper close off one corridor of the old courthouse in an even row.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.venue_room: Ancien Palais de Justice, hanging from ceiling
works.title: The Fabric of Identity
works.what_you_see: Aluminium copies of passports from fictional countries hang from the ceiling. To see what is written, a visitor must stop, look up and decode the text.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.title: Map-elective
works.what_you_see: Paper maps are cut and sculpted by braiding and locking into an immersive installation in the courtyard of the courthouse. It is called a collective project and it echoes the braided hair shown in Lizette Nin's work nearby.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.venue_room: Former Supreme Court chamber, Ancien Palais de Justice
works.title: A Palace in Pieces
works.what_you_see: A site-specific intervention in the old Supreme Court chamber, where trials and uprisings happened, shown with two videos from the early 2000s. A second work, Mountain Mama (2024), shows ancestral and modern feminine figures in an Afrofuturist underwater world.
claims: Critic: the most effective use of the building's colonial memory.

works.exhibition: 15th Dak'Art, Dakar Biennale: The Wake (L'Eveil, Le Sillage, Xall wi)
works.title: Haptic Library
works.what_you_see: A room for rest and study set up like an improvised living room. It is the main shared and participatory space in the show. It is part of the Archive Ensemble research group's work.
claims: Critic: keeps a temporary but close community together.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.title: Air of Firozabad/Air of Palestine
works.what_you_see: Hundreds of glass baubles, blown in Firozabad (India) and in Palestine, hang on clear wire over the heads of visitors. They seem ready to fall and shatter at any moment.
claims: Makes felt how people are vulnerable to harm from the air, from pollution or war.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.title: Parliament of Ghosts
works.what_you_see: A chamber is draped in jute sacks sewn together by Kochi homemakers, with a forest of mended wooden chairs rescued from public institutions inside. Local carpenters repaired the chairs. The room also works as a place for discussion and performance.
nonvisual: performance and talks are held inside
claims: Recalls colonial spaces of government and the trade behind their curtains.
Part of the artist's idea of objects as documents.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.venue_room: Anand Warehouse (dark room next to Mahama)
works.title: Shelter: for the time being
works.what_you_see: A dark, cave-like room. Visitors get torches and walk along suspended scrolls made of paper, grass, jute, metal and seed pods. The torch beams throw shadows on the walls like rock shelter paintings.
claims: Shadows recall the Bhimbetka rock shelters.
Beauty comes when one faces one's shadows.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.title: Only the Earth Knows Their Labor
works.what_you_see: Hand-made ceramic tools and torsos are displayed against a brick wall that points to the brick kilns of Uttar Pradesh.
claims: Shows the effect of hard labour on the bodies of migrant workers.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.title: Barakah
works.what_you_see: An ark-like community kitchen made of Kerala timber and thatch. It was still being built when the biennale opened.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.title: Indelible Black Marks
works.what_you_see: A film shows the artist and helpers in white running synchronised routes through a Punjab rice field on fire, dragging long white cotton banners. Around the film hang canvases that are singed and rubbed with soot, ash and straw.
nonvisual: scent: aromatic soot from the canvases
claims: Draws attention to disempowered farmers and the pollution caused by stubble burning.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.venue_room: 111 Markaz and Cafe, disused building overrun by a banyan tree
works.title: Soft Offerings to Scorched Lands and the Brokenhearted
works.what_you_see: An open-ended garden grows inside a disused building taken over by a large banyan tree, next to a canal. A soundscape by Nithin Shamsuddin plays over it.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.venue_room: Aspinwall House, by the sea; behind curtains
works.title: Omens Drawn by Lightning
works.what_you_see: Bodies move in a rhythm that is part free and part set, behind curtains placed so that viewers can peep in. It is a series of installation-performances that blur prayer, movement and installation.
claims: Positioned as a tirade against rational, extractive, Eurocentric ways of knowing; offers Indigenous knowledge, occult medicine and ritual instead.

works.exhibition: 6th Kochi-Muziris Biennale: For the Time Being
works.venue_room: Aspinwall House, a room in the colonial-era mansion
works.title: Male Bust (c. 1933); Nude Man with Column (c. 1935); Young Man with Sickle (c. 1938)
works.what_you_see: A room of black-and-white photographs of young Sri Lankan men, farmers and fishermen among them, shown in a corner of a colonial mansion. The bodies are lit like tender sculpture, with light and sweat.
claims: Made in the 1930s when homosexuality was criminal under British colonial law; read as celebrating the working male body.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.venue_room: 'Water and Habitats' hall, dim room under a spotlight
works.title: Mineral Lick
works.what_you_see: A length of fabric hangs from above under one spotlight in a dim hall, with its tail trailing like a bridal train. The cloth was soaked in dye, salt and water gathered from all 60 sectors of Beirut.
claims: The artist calls it an abstract hydromap of water toxicity in Beirut.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.title: Tuban
works.what_you_see: Glass beakers drip distilled spices and leaves, such as cinnamon and sandalwood, onto open books about policies that allowed colonial plunder. The title is a port town that was an Islamic culture hub from the 13th to early 16th century.
claims: Shows what was lost and how it was taken (the artist calls the Dutch plunder extractivist greed).

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.title: Turathuna (Our Tradition)
works.what_you_see: A series of 39 small white panels, each with one woman at the middle in traditional dress from across Saudi Arabia. Every detail was researched: dyed cloth, gold silk thread, jewellery, straw hat.
claims: Gives factual, generous record of dress; a critic reads it as a eulogy for folk heritage.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.title: In Lieu of What Was
works.what_you_see: Five very large water containers cast in clear lacquered fibreglass stand like canopic jars. They glow like alabaster at pharaonic scale.
claims: Prompts thought on the politics of water in a region of conflict and climate stress.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.venue_room: Entry hall and a second room, hanging
works.title: Logoligi Logarithm
works.what_you_see: A gold curtain of aluminium and copper wire hangs from the ceiling in 66 free parts, forming a maze of metal that visitors walk in and out of. A second Anatsui hangs opposite the main entrance.
claims: Title is borrowed from a poem book by Atukwei Okai: 'Logoligi' in Ga means snake-like or indirect.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2024: After Rain
works.title: An Equation of State
works.what_you_see: Mangrove saplings are raised and lowered by machine into a tank of water.
claims: Comments on habitat loss near Bantayan island, Philippines.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
works.title: The Source
works.what_you_see: Circular modules refer to aerial views of centre-pivot irrigation. Water tanks and green PVC pipes for drinking water and white pipes for wastewater are left exposed. It is a public drinking fountain.
claims: Makes the logic of water distribution visible; follows field research in Al Ahsa oasis and its 2,000-year-old irrigation canal system.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
works.title: AGBA: 8 Stone Cave
works.what_you_see: A sacred-architectural structure with an outer skin of light fabric made by the artist, over a clay-brick frame called the bone. The fabric carries geometric Al-Qatt Al-Asiri patterns, plant and herb motifs, a turtle shell and a weaver bird.
claims: Honours the passing of ancestral knowledge; links the Yoruba idea of abba (elders) with Saudi women's wall painting.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
works.title: Pavilion Prototype III: Camera Obscura #0 Mafadi
works.what_you_see: A timber camera obscura. Visitors enter what looks like the inside of a camera, where near and far images pass across suspended translucent screens.
nonvisual: light: projected images in a dark chamber
claims: Mafadi means salt in Khelobedu; the work links salt, desalination and rain-making.
The pavilion is a porous archive.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
works.title: Con-junto and Ambulancia
works.what_you_see: Huge scrap-metal sculptures reach toward the ceiling of an aircraft-hangar space. Discarded materials are turned into mythic figures.
claims: Critic: staged forensically, they risk becoming relics of energy.

works.exhibition: Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale 2026: In Interludes and Transitions
works.title: Years of the Shining Face
works.what_you_see: Coloured curtains form a theatre-like architecture around a fibreglass face on a plinth.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.venue_room: Hallenbad Ost (disused swimming pool), Friedrichsplatz, Rondell, C&A facade
works.title: Bara Solidaritas: Sekarang Mereka, Besok Kita (Flame of Solidarity: First they came for them, then they came for us)
works.what_you_see: A mural, large banners and many life-size cardboard puppets (wayang kardus) are shown in a disused swimming pool venue and outdoors; puppets stand outside the pool entrance. Workshops, carnival and music events go with them. A banner on Friedrichsplatz was covered and then taken down after a row over antisemitic imagery.
claims: Collective says it follows three principles: organise, educate, agitate.
Practice mixes street protest, woodcut workshops, art carnivals and shows in unusual spaces.
references: Taring Padi, founded 1998 by art students and activists in Indonesia's reformation era

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.title: Tuan Mami, Vietnamese Immigrating Garden
works.what_you_see: A garden of migratory plant species made with money and gifts from Vietnamese immigrants in Germany. A wooden shed holds a seed library where people can leave or take seeds. The review counted 16 builders, 36 donors and 50 takers on the day.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.title: Return to Sender
works.what_you_see: E-waste is sorted by colour into monochrome free-standing cubes. Used clothes are bound tight, bundled and stacked into an enclosure. Inside, a video called Delivery Details shows second-hand clothing in Nairobi.
nonvisual: video: Return to Sender - Delivery Details
claims: Shows how the Global North ships its problems to the Global South.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.title: Rasad - Food Objects, Local Bazaar and Supershop
works.medium_line: Ceramic, metal, fabric, cotton, natural spices, and seeds
works.what_you_see: A kiosk-like shop of ceramic and crocheted foods, made sinister by torpedo-like fish and pineapple grenades. Next to it hangs a big mural, Chayachobi, of Bengali film scenes about food crises. Outside, a pergola garden leads to an open-air kitchen where visitors can volunteer to cook.
claims: Looks at food as identity, trauma and community.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.artist: Michel Lafleur and Tom Bogaert (with Atis Rezistans | Ghetto Biennale)
works.title: Famasi Mobil Kongole .01
works.medium_line: Electric lights, Congo Blue filter sheets, hand painted cardboard, plastic buckets, multicolored pills, rubber bands, and pairs of scissors
works.dimensions: 80 x 60 x 40 cm (Blue); 150 x 60 x 30 cm (Yellow); 70 x 40 x 40 cm (Red); 180 x 50 x 30 cm (White)
works.what_you_see: Columns hung with blister packs of medicine, fairy lights and tinsel, like shrines, stand in a Catholic church. Sculptures by other group members, such as wheel-cap haloes made of scrap metal, tires and car parts, share the nave.
claims: Recalls mobile pharmacies in Haiti; ties vodou practice to the church setting.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.venue_room: Hubner Areal, ground floor, a 'land office' room
works.title: Clay Workshop
works.what_you_see: A giant sphere of clay bricks stands in a hall next to the way to a room set up as an office. A representative sells visitors 4 x 4 metre plots of Java forest, each with a terracotta brick and an NFT certificate, to build a collectively owned forest.
claims: Aims to beat developers by buying land together.

works.exhibition: documenta fifteen
works.artist_born: Sudanese artist; Trampoline House is in Copenhagen
works.title: The Walls Have Ears
works.what_you_see: A series of listening posts in a pedestrian tunnel play the stories of asylum seekers in Denmark.
claims: Amplifies voices that are not heard.

works.exhibition: Bangkok Art Biennale 2024: Nurture Gaia
works.title: A Conversation with a Potter
works.what_you_see: Rooms look like an archaeology museum: careful arrangement, museum lighting, a skeleton embracing a three-legged pot. The unglazed pots are shaped by hand from clay dug at Bangkok construction sites, set in precise rows.
claims: Links urban growth upward with digging into the past.

works.exhibition: Bangkok Art Biennale 2024: Nurture Gaia
works.title: Mapping the Land Body Stories of its Past
works.what_you_see: A machine with a brush paints Indonesian forest on a big canvas, then releases water to wash it away, and starts again. A bio-electric power source is a palm tree beside the work.
claims: A metaphor for the exploitation of nature by industry.

works.exhibition: Bangkok Art Biennale 2024: Nurture Gaia
works.title: Fish, Fire, Fallout
works.what_you_see: Seven sculpted fish stand in a glass case that has text etched into it. A video shows a chef frying tilapia, with images from an old Thai text about the end of the world. The museum lent artefacts to sit beside it.
claims: Connects history, myth, politics and ecology in one collage.
